uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast prices paid by UK households are rising. It is the figure the Bank of England's 2% target is set against, and it feeds into benefit, pension and rail-fare upratings.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The September reading arrives as economists warn that UK inflation would reach 5% if a US diesel ban goes ahead, a reminder of how directly fuel costs pass into British prices. The release sets the baseline that warning is measured from: where prices stood before any such shock.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target for overnight lending between US banks. Its decisions move borrowing costs wherever debt is priced in dollars, at home and abroad.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs in September against 90,000 expected, a stall that lands on a committee traders had priced for a run of rate hikes. The meeting settles whether weak hiring interrupts that path. It convenes with Trump demanding Powell's resignation after a watchdog cleared him over building renovations.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries that share the euro. Its decisions reach mortgages, business loans and the euro's exchange rate.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, days after Lagarde painted a darkening picture of prices in Europe. With business activity at a 3½-year high, rate-setters cannot cite a weak economy as a reason to wait. This meeting settles whether that pressure becomes a hike.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its rate has long been the lowest of any major economy, so its moves reach the yen and everyone worldwide who borrows in it.
boj-2026-10.recent: Three sources told Reuters the bank may say this month that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2% target. For a decade it justified near-zero rates by arguing that inflation was still short of that mark, so dropping the line removes its own stated reason to hold. At stake is the yen, which cheap Japanese rates have held down.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote feeds through to UK mortgage and savings rates, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee votes on whether to move the rate that the country's mortgages, savings accounts and business loans are priced from. Nothing reported so far sets this meeting apart from a routine one.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the range for overnight lending between US banks. Its decisions move the dollar and borrowing costs worldwide.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Hiring has stalled: the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs in September against 90,000 expected. Yet traders had priced in 4 rate hikes by June 2027, so the committee is weighing a weak labour market against pressure to raise. It decides with Trump demanding Powell resign, after a watchdog cleared him.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from 19 major economies plus the European Union and African Union, hosted by a rotating presidency that sets the agenda. Its members produce about 85% of world output, and it decides by consensus.
g20-2026-miami.recent: Rubio has invited Putin, who is wanted by the ICC, to Miami, and the Kremlin is weighing the invitation. Its answer sets what the summit is about before any agenda item: whether the other leaders sit at a table with him, and whether a host's invitation counts for more than the court's.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council sets interest rates for the countries that share the euro, meeting roughly every six weeks. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs from German mortgages to Italian government debt.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, the highest level in three years, and Lagarde has painted a darkening picture of prices in Europe. Business activity is at a 3½-year high, so the council has no slowdown to set against the pressure to hike. This meeting settles whether it treats the jump as lasting.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which votes eight times a year on Bank Rate. The rate feeds through to British mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee votes on the interest rate that British lenders price mortgages and business loans from. The decision settles what borrowing costs households and firms carry into the new year.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its rate anchors the yen and the cost of the cheap borrowing that funds investments far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Three sources told Reuters the bank is weighing a statement that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2% target, the shortfall it cited for a decade to keep rates near zero. With that argument gone, the board has to justify holding on other grounds, and the answer reaches the yen and the borrowers worldwide who fund themselves in it.

fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what US households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. It is the inflation reading that moves Treasury yields, the dollar and expectations for Federal Reserve policy.
fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.recent: This release shows how much of the Middle East energy shock has reached US prices. It lands on a Fed whose case for raising rates now rests on inflation alone: the Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs in September against 90,000 expected. Higher rates also fall on a Treasury paying about $1 trillion a year in interest.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Producer Price Index, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures what US producers receive for goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop prices, and bond yields and the dollar move with it.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what American shops, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so the figure moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
